must: Keep color-scheme: dark — this is a committed identity ("Meridian", decision D12), not a light/dark toggle
Reuse the existing token set (--background/--card/--primary as white-pill CTA/--ring as the only blue accent) rather than introducing new brand colors
Reuse existing installed shadcn primitives (button, card, dialog, input, label, skeleton, sonner, textarea) before adding a new one
Optimize for dense, scannable data (tables, findings, multi-stage review flows), not generous marketing whitespace
avoid: Decorative motion, scroll-driven animation, parallax, or any 'awwwards-style' flourish — CLAUDE.md: clarity and professional credibility over visual flourish
Consumer/marketing visual language (hero sections, big illustration, gradients-as-decoration, glassmorphism)
New color hues beyond the existing near-black/white/blue-accent/muted-red-destructive palette
Playful or informal tone in copy or iconography — this is a diligence tool used by analysts and deal leads

decisions.decision: Adopted Direction A (persistent sidebar shell) for frontend/ navigation, reimplemented from the Sidebar (id 1075, https://21st.dev/@manuarora700/components/sidebar) and Sidebar Dashboard Skeleton (id 19009) references rather than installed verbatim - the reference was Next.js + framer-motion with hover-only expand (no keyboard path); rebuilt as click-toggled, CSS-transition-only, styled from the existing --sidebar-* tokens, using react-router Link.

Direction B (dense filterable/sortable tables) for findings/documents. Found during scoping that findings (static/workspace.html/js) already had this exact pattern - search, 6 filters, sortable columns, severity/origin badges - built in Milestone 9, well before this design exploration started. Documents (static/project.html/js) did not: added search + folder/type filters + sortable columns (Name/Folder/Type/Size/Uploaded) + a count hint, mirroring the exact filters/sortState/visibleX() idiom findings already used. Generalized the shared filter-bar and sortable-table-header CSS out of workspace.css into style.css (.filter-bar/.filter-field/.filter-actions, .documents-table th[data-sort]) so both pages use one definition instead of two drifting copies; kept the sticky-positioning behavior opt-in (.filter-bar-sticky) since workspace.html is a dedicated page but project.html is one card among several.

Direction C (status-first board) for the mandate list. Grouped mandates into columns by lifecycle status (draft/awaiting_approval/active/under_review/completed/cancelled/failed - "planning" excluded, declared in mandates.py but never actually reachable). No drag-and-drop: status changes already happen via explicit actions on the mandate detail page, never from the list, so the board is a read-only grouped view of the same clickable cards - this sidesteps the kanban drag-accessibility risk entirely rather than needing a keyboard-operable alternative to dragging. Desktop: horizontal scrolling row of columns. Mobile: stacked full-width sections, not horizontal-scroll-only. Empty columns show explicit "No mandates" text rather than being hidden, so the whole pipeline shape is visible at a glance.
decisions.revertReason: Founder saw it live and didn't like the look - reverted MandateList.tsx to the flat list (STATUS_LABELS pill per row), same as before this decision. No other Direction C infrastructure existed elsewhere to unwind.
